A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LongVILA and MM-SP. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures and tables, are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v4 reports original video and image benchmark results, needle-retrieval experiments, captioning evaluations, ablations, and training/inference measurements.

after.justification: v6 retains original empirical results and adds video benchmark evaluations, training-schedule comparisons, a smaller model evaluation, and computational profiling.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 retain the five-stage curriculum, data-generation procedure, two-stage image/token sharding, 2D-attention communication, and distributed inference. The additional model size and alternative training schedules extend evaluation without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v6 Table 3 adds evaluations on ActivityNet-QA, EgoSchema, EventBench, LongVideoBench, PerceptionTest, MVBench, NExT-QA, and VNBench, substantially broadening video dataset coverage. VideoMME, needle retrieval, LongVILA-Caption, and the ten image benchmarks remain. Captioning moves to Appendix A.1.

E2.justification: v6 Table 3 adds VideoMME comparisons with GPT-4V, GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, VideoLLaMA2.1, and LLaVA-OV, plus Flash-VStream and PLLaVA comparisons on added benchmarks. The original VideoMME comparator set remains in Table 4; systems and image-benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated model configurations from Qwen2-7B plus Llama3-8B ablations to Qwen2-1.5B/7B. Evaluation introduces training-order/joint-training controls and extends frame sweeps to 1,024. Table 10 adds component profiling across two model sizes and 32-512 frames using fp16 and Flash-Attention2 on one A100. Existing distributed-system protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 Table 4's Stage 3/4 omission ablation is replaced by training-order and joint-SFT comparisons in v6 Table 1. The frame-scaling analysis now focuses on long VideoMME with and without subtitles; v4 Figure 2's short/medium and dense captioning sweeps disappear. Table 10 adds component-cost analysis. The three-point captioning test and original systems/convergence analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging throughput over five iterations after ten warmup iterations in Section 5.1.1. Neither supplies independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Added results continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: For the reported 7B, 256-frame VideoMME configuration, overall scores change from 57.4/61.8 without/with subtitles in v4 Table 3 to 60.1/65.1 in v6 Table 4; the cause is not explained. v6 adds eight benchmark result sets, 1.5B scores, schedule comparisons, and profiling measurements, and revises frame-sweep results. The 99.8% needle result and captioning table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the existing attention/sharding reasoning is retained. v6 Table 10 adds computational profiling and scaling interpretation without introducing a formal derivation or mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the accuracy claim from VideoMME to nine video benchmarks and update the headline score to 65.1%. Captioning loses its headline emphasis but remains supported in the appendix. The central five-stage/MM-SP contribution and million-token retrieval and training-scale claims remain.

C2.justification: v6 Table 10 newly interprets attention's quadratic cost growth, versus other components' linear growth, as the dominant computational bottleneck motivating MM-SP. Existing interpretations of captioning improvements, workload balance, networking limitations, and convergence are retained.

D1.justification: v6 adds profiling hardware, precision, attention implementation, component definitions, and parameter counts in Table 10. It explicitly states code/model availability and changes the repository access target. Figure 1 drops the specific 1,024-frame Stage 5 training statement, without establishing an actual training change. Most existing training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 adds references for new benchmarks, comparators, and Flash-Attention2, and removes the Llama 3 model-card reference. Section 5.3 adds a qualified claim to being the first VLM handling one-million-token context. The related-work discussion positioning LongVILA against VILA, USP, and LoongTrain is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact. Local edits rename Sections 2 and 5, remove a duplicated networking paragraph, revise the abstract/conclusion, and move LongVILA-Caption from Section 5.4 to Appendix A.1. The first two authors exchange order.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: v4's two-panel Figure 2 is replaced by a long-video subtitle comparison, the needle plot moves earlier, and the training-ablation table is redesigned. New benchmark and component-profiling tables are added, while captioning and sharding tables move into the appendix. Most system diagrams and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially strengthens empirical support for the full-stack proposal. Table 3 addresses v4's narrow VideoMME-centered video comparison, while Tables 1 and 10 test training-order choices and quantify computational bottlenecks. Captioning and original systems evidence are preserved. Removing the stage-omission ablation loses a useful control, and experimental documentation and uncertainty reporting remain limited, but the broader validation and computational analysis provide a substantial net improvement.
